chunks: Muhammad ibn Ismail from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who borrowed wealth, and a year passed over it while it was in his possession, he (peace be upon him) said: 'If the one who lent it to him pays its zakat, then there is no zakat upon him; and if he does not pay, the borrower pays.'
ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for paying zakat on borrowed money?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the mechanism of double taxation avoidance in Zakat by linking the borrower's liability to the lender's status, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that Zakat is a single obligation on the wealth's owner. It highlights the practical implication that the borrower must verify the lender's payment or assume the duty themselves, ensuring the wealth's Zakat is fulfilled regardless of possession. This ruling underscores the communal responsibility in maintaining the purity of wealth within the Islamic economic system.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Mansour Bin Hazim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah

asws regarding a man who borrow some wealth, and a year passes by over it and it is still in his possession. Heasws said: ‘If it was so that then one who lent it to him did pay his Zakāt, so there would be no Zakāt upon him; but if it was so that he had not paid, the borrower would pay’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mansur ibn Hazim who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who borrows a certain amount of wealth and it remains with him for one year. He (the Imam) said, ‘If the person from whom he has borrowed pays Zakat for such wealth then Zakat is not due on the borrower but if the lender does not pay then he (the borrower) pays Zakat for such wealth.’”
